guide.anim.curves.p1: The Curve Editor offers multi-channel curve editing (.curve.json): each channel has a name, color and visibility; keys support linear / cubic / constant interpolation plus in/out tangent editing.
guide.anim.curves.p2: The Timeline tab is a clip-preview transport for the focused entity: it shows the bound entity and current clip, with Play/Pause, step, jump-to-start/end buttons plus speed, loop and a multi-clip dropdown.
guide.anim.curves.s1: Create channels with '+ Add Channel' and switch the active channel, visibility, color and name in the channel table; 'Remove Active' deletes the active channel.
guide.anim.curves.s2: Click the canvas to add keys and drag to adjust; with a key selected, edit time / value / tangents and interpolation under 'Selected Key'. 'Flatten' zeroes the tangents, 'Auto' takes the slope between the neighboring keys.
guide.anim.curves.s3: 'Frame All' refits the viewport to all visible keys; the mouse wheel zooms (Shift = horizontal only, Ctrl = vertical only) and middle-drag pans.
guide.anim.curves.s4: Fill in 'File (.curve.json)' to 'Save / Load'; 'Clear' resets every channel to two keys.
guide.anim.curves.s5: Select an entity with an animation component, then click or drag on the ruler to scrub pose by pose — changes here write straight back into the component's playback state.
guide.anim.curves.tip1: Timeline, Inspector and Animation Editor share the same component playback state: press Play in any of them and the others follow.
guide.anim.curves.title: Curve Editor & Timeline
guide.anim.curves.warn1: .curve.json is currently an editor-side utility asset with no direct runtime consumer — to drive entity properties at runtime, use the Sequencer instead (.seq.json + Sequence Player).
guide.anim.ik.p1: The Animation Rigging tab edits the IK constraint stack of the focused entity. Constraints live in the entity's 'IK Constraints' component — real scene data, serialized with the scene; 'Two Bone IK' is solved at runtime right after pose sampling.
guide.anim.ik.s1: Select an entity with a Skeletal Animator (or an Avatar component) — otherwise the panel asks you to pick a valid target first.
guide.anim.ik.s2: Click 'Add Constraint'. New constraints default to 'Two Bone IK' with weight 1.0 and enabled; the component is created on demand.
guide.anim.ik.s3: Fill in 'Root / Mid / End Bone': a bone dropdown when an Avatar is bound, otherwise type the joint name (resolved by name in the skeleton at runtime).
guide.anim.ik.s4: Drag an entity from the Hierarchy onto the 'Target Entity' button as the IK goal; optionally drag a 'Pole Entity' to steer the elbow/knee, or use the 'Pole Offset' vector when there is no pole entity.
guide.anim.ik.s5: Control the constraint with the 'Weight' slider (0 to 1) and the 'Enabled' checkbox; X removes a single constraint.
guide.anim.ik.tip1: The 'IK Constraints' card in the Inspector shows the constraint count and offers an 'Open Animation Rigging' button that jumps straight to this tab.
guide.anim.ik.title: IK & Animation Rigging
guide.anim.ik.warn1: Only 'Two Bone IK' is solved at runtime today; the Aim / Multi-Parent / Position / Rotation kinds can be authored and round-trip with the scene, but are not solved yet.
guide.anim.ik.warn2: Without a Skeletal Animator driving the skinned pose the constraint stack is inert — the panel calls this out in yellow.
guide.anim.sequencer.hk1: Enter Play mode to verify runtime playback
guide.anim.sequencer.p1: The Sequencer authors multi-track timelines (.seq.json): property tracks (scalar, linear interpolation), event tracks (markers only) and color tracks (RGB). Tracks can be bound to scene entity properties, and scrubbing previews the result live in the scene.
guide.anim.sequencer.s1: Add tracks with '+ Property Track / + Event Track / + Color Track', then set 'Duration' and 'FPS' (FPS controls keyframe snapping).
guide.anim.sequencer.s2: Select a track, drag an entity from the Hierarchy onto 'Bind Entity', then pick the driven property in the 'Bind Property' dropdown.
guide.anim.sequencer.s3: Add keys in the track lane, or edit time and value precisely in the key table below; drag the 'Playhead' to watch the scene update live in edit mode.
guide.anim.sequencer.s4: Fill in 'Path' and click 'Save' to write the .seq.json.
guide.anim.sequencer.s5: Select the entity that should own the sequence and click 'Sync to Player': it writes the sequence path and per-track entity bindings into its Sequence Player component (undoable). In Play mode and in shipped builds the runtime drives the sequence.
guide.anim.sequencer.tip1: Live preview runs only in edit mode (stopped); the panel caches every original value it touches and restores them on Stop, on tab switch and before scene save.
guide.anim.sequencer.title: Sequencer
guide.anim.sequencer.warn1: 'Sync to Player' requires a selected entity and a saved path first — otherwise the Console warns and nothing is written.
guide.anim.skeletal.p1: The Skeletal Animator component plays the skeletal animation that ships inside a model. It consumes a model file containing a skeleton and animation clips (glTF/GLB recommended); clip names are read straight from the model, with up to 8 clips listed per component.
guide.anim.skeletal.s1: Select the entity that should play the animation in the Hierarchy.
guide.anim.skeletal.s2: Click 'Add Component' at the bottom of the Inspector, then search for and add 'Skeletal Animator'.
guide.anim.skeletal.s3: Drag a .glb / .gltf model from the Asset Browser onto the 'Skeleton' field, or pick it via the browse button (the dialog filters to model assets).
guide.anim.skeletal.s4: The component automatically reads the clip names from the model; switch the playing clip with the 'Active Clip' dropdown.
guide.anim.skeletal.s5: Adjust 'Speed' and 'Loop', then press 'Play' to preview in the Scene view; the progress bar below shows current time vs. clip duration.
guide.anim.skeletal.tip1: The same component has a built-in 1D blend tree: enable 'Blend Tree (1D)' and the 'Blend Param' cross-blends between per-clip thresholds — the classic use is blending walk/run by movement speed. The first enable seeds an ascending threshold spread automatically.
guide.anim.skeletal.title: Skeletal Animation Basics
guide.anim.skeletal.warn1: The model must carry its own skeleton and animation data; prefer glTF/GLB. Clip names are the model's internal names — the state machine and frame events both match by this exact name.
guide.anim.sm.p1: An animator state machine (.anim_sm.json) switches clips automatically by parameter conditions: each state references a clip, transitions carry conditions plus a blend duration, and the parameter table holds Float / Int / Bool / Trigger parameters.
guide.anim.sm.p2: The state machine is only driven in Play mode; in edit mode you still preview via 'Active Clip'. Once bound, the Inspector shows the current state name and live controls for every parameter — drag floats, tick bools or hit Trigger buttons during Play to verify transitions.
guide.anim.sm.s1: Right-click empty canvas and choose 'New State'; right-click an existing state to 'Make Default', 'Add Transition...' or 'Delete'. Pan with middle-mouse drag, zoom with Ctrl+wheel.
guide.anim.sm.s2: Select a state and fill in its name and 'Clip' in the State section on the right — just type the model's clip name; matching is case-insensitive and ignores paths. Each state also has its own speed and looping.
guide.anim.sm.s3: After 'Add Transition', click the target state to finish the edge; click an edge to select the transition and set 'Duration' (the crossfade blend time), 'Has Exit Time' and the condition list.
guide.anim.sm.s4: Add parameters with '+ Param' in the table at the bottom; a condition is parameter + operator + threshold, with true/false operators for Bool/Trigger.
guide.anim.sm.s5: Fill in 'Path' and click 'Save' to write the .anim_sm.json; then bind it in the Inspector by entering (or dragging) it into the Skeletal Animator's 'State Machine' field.
guide.anim.sm.tip1: Transitions are true crossfades: the from/to clips are sampled together, weighted by the blend — no hard pose switch.
guide.anim.sm.tip2: Speed, IsGrounded, VerticalVel and Jump are reserved engine parameter names: when the component's autoSpeed field is enabled (a scene-data field; no Inspector toggle yet) the runtime feeds them from movement and physics automatically. Otherwise parameters are driven entirely by game code or the Inspector's manual controls.
guide.anim.sm.tip3: The panel has its own undo/redo (toolbar buttons, or Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y while the panel is focused), independent of the scene undo stack.
guide.anim.sm.title: Animator State Machine
guide.anim.sm.warn1: Fill in 'Path' before 'Load'; 'Save' resolves through the asset path system and lands where the engine actually reads it, not the process working directory.
guide.anim.title: Animation
guide.anim.workbench.p1: Animation tools live in the Animation Editor workbench: one window with six tabs — Animation Editor (frame events), Animator State Machine, Curve Editor, Sequencer, Timeline and Animation Rigging. The matching Window-menu entries jump straight to the corresponding tab.
guide.anim.workbench.p2: The Animation Editor tab edits the frame-event sidecar <skeleton path>.anim.json: each track maps to one clip, and the diamonds on a track are events carrying a time, an optional name and a numeric payload (Event ID, F0, F1, I0). At runtime they are dispatched to game code as playback advances.
guide.anim.workbench.s1: Select an entity with a Skeletal Animator and click 'Sync Clips From Selection' — the panel creates one identically-named track per clip.
guide.anim.workbench.s2: Double-click an empty spot on a track to add an event at that time; drag a diamond to move it; right-click a diamond to delete it.
guide.anim.workbench.s3: Edit the selected event's name, Event ID, F0/F1, I0 and time in the inspector pane on the right.
guide.anim.workbench.s4: Click 'Save'. The default path is derived automatically as <skeleton path>.anim.json — exactly where the runtime looks it up.
guide.anim.workbench.tip1: Once you edit the 'File' path by hand it stops following the selection (it becomes a Save-As); 'Duration' and 'Loop' are panel preview settings only — the engine uses the model clip's real duration.
guide.anim.workbench.tip2: The toolbar's Play/Pause/Stop and the 'Zoom' slider drive the in-panel preview; click or drag the ruler at the top to scrub the time cursor.
guide.anim.workbench.title: Animation Workbench & Frame Events
guide.anim.workbench.warn1: A track name must match the model clip name exactly (case-sensitive), otherwise that track's events never fire at runtime.
guide.assets.browser.b1: Locations sidebar: drives, home, desktop, documents, downloads, plus favorites — click "+" to add the current folder, right-click a favorite to remove it.
guide.assets.browser.b2: Breadcrumb bar: Up, project root, Browse… (OS folder picker), Set Root; every path segment is clickable for direct navigation.
guide.assets.browser.b3: View toggle: Grid (colored type tiles) or Details (name / date modified / type / size columns); the chosen view is persisted.
guide.assets.browser.b4: The search box searches all subdirectories of the current folder recursively (capped at 500 results); the type dropdown on its left filters by Images / Models / Audio / Code / Archive.
guide.assets.browser.b5: Double-click: folders open in place; .scene files load straight into the editor; everything else opens in the File Viewer.
guide.assets.browser.b6: With the file area focused, type a letter or digit to jump to the first entry starting with it; pressing the same key again within 1.5 s cycles through matches (same as Windows Explorer).
guide.assets.browser.hk1: Show / hide the Asset Browser panel
guide.assets.browser.p1: The Asset Browser browses your project folder directly on disk — there is no separate import database; the files themselves are the assets. When you open a project the browser root follows the project root; the panel polls for directory changes every 0.35 s, so files added outside the editor appear automatically.
guide.assets.browser.p2: The panel has two columns: the Locations sidebar and project directory tree on the left, and the breadcrumb bar, search bar and file area on the right.
guide.assets.browser.tip1: File tiles are drag sources — drop them onto the Scene view or a path field in the Inspector to reference the asset.
guide.assets.browser.tip2: Right-click a folder → "Set as Project Root" is only a temporary browsing sandbox; scene rendering, Play and packaging still follow the real project root. Use "Restore Project Root" to return.
guide.assets.browser.title: Asset Browser
guide.assets.bundles.b1: Shared threshold: assets referenced by the configured number of scenes (default 2) or more move into the shared bundle automatically, avoiding duplicate shipping.
guide.assets.bundles.b2: Cook assets: textures become GPU block-compressed .jceasset (BC or ASTC per target platform), models become GLB+meshopt, audio becomes PCM.
guide.assets.bundles.b3: Zstd compression level 1–22; enabling "Encrypt" (ChaCha20) generates the project key on the spot if none exists yet.
guide.assets.bundles.b4: Path independence: references outside the asset root are virtualized to _external/<hash>_<filename>; .jcol and .anim.json sidecars keep their suffix relationship with their base asset; the i18n/ localization tables under the source asset folder ship wholesale.
guide.assets.bundles.hk1: Queue the current scene for single-scene packing
guide.assets.bundles.p1: Bundles are shipping-oriented asset packages (.jbundle + bundle_catalog.json). The packer parses every asset reference key in the scene JSON (meshes / materials / textures / audio / scripts / animation and more) and recursively scans textures referenced by material files — all scene dependencies are packed automatically, no manual manifest.
guide.assets.bundles.p2: The Build tab offers three modes: Project (scans the whole project, with incremental and shared bundles), Selected scenes (hand-picked scene files), and Single scene (one self-contained .jbundle, no catalog).
guide.assets.bundles.p3: File → Open Bundle loads a .jbundle or bundle_catalog.json as the scene source, previewing the scene exactly as it will load at runtime.
guide.assets.bundles.s2: Choose File → Pack Current Scene as Bundle; the Build tab switches to single-scene mode with the scene path pre-filled.
guide.assets.bundles.s3: Click "Pack Scene". Packing runs on a background thread; progress and logs stream into the Console.
guide.assets.bundles.s4: On the Browse tab, enter the bundle_catalog.json path and click Refresh to verify each bundle's size, entry count, refcount and dependencies.
guide.assets.bundles.tip1: The "Scene dependency preview" section can run a dependency scan on a single scene file and print the full dependency list to the Console — handy for a pre-pack check.
guide.assets.bundles.title: Building Bundles and Browsing Them
guide.assets.bundles.warn1: Scenes loaded from a bundle are read-only — Save is ignored; go back to the source project to make changes.
guide.assets.bundles.warn2: Encryption only deters casual extraction: the decryption key ships inside the game binary, so do not treat it as strong protection.
guide.assets.import.b1: Texture presets: target format (rgba8 / bc1 / bc3 / bc7), generate mipmaps, sRGB, max size.
guide.assets.import.b2: Model presets: scale, generate normals / tangents, flip UV, merge meshes, and collider generation (mode / split / static).
guide.assets.import.b3: glTF / GLB rows have an "Inspect" button: it parses and counts nodes / meshes / primitives / materials / animations / skins, and lists unresolved external image references — a health check before importing.
guide.assets.import.p1: Adding assets to the project = putting files into the project folder: copy them in your OS file manager, or use the context menu "Open in Explorer" to jump to the target folder; the Asset Browser refreshes automatically.
guide.assets.import.p2: Import Presets declare import parameters in bulk: they write a sidecar file <asset>.import.json next to each asset, consumed by the packaging cook and the import pipeline. It lives as a tab of the Asset Pipeline workbench (Bundle Browser).
guide.assets.import.s1: Click "New Preset", name it, choose its kind (Texture or Model), and configure the parameters.
guide.assets.import.s2: Click "Save All" to persist the presets to editor/presets/import_presets.json.
guide.assets.import.s3: In "Asset Scan", enter a scan root and click "Scan"; the table lists every texture / model with its sidecar status, filterable by name, kind, or "only missing".
guide.assets.import.s4: With a preset selected, click "Apply" per row, or use "Apply to visible rows" to write .import.json sidecars in bulk.
guide.assets.import.tip1: When packaging cooks textures it reads target_format, mipmap and related settings from the sidecar and outputs the matching GPU compressed format.
guide.assets.import.title: Importing Assets and Import Presets
guide.assets.import.warn1: Model sidecar parameters such as scale / normals are consumed by the editor importer; the bundle-time GLB conversion does not apply them.
guide.assets.manage.b1: Open with: Open (folders navigate / files go to the viewer), Open in VS Code, Open in Explorer, Open in Terminal.
guide.assets.manage.b2: File operations: Rename, Duplicate, Copy Path, plus Copy / Cut / Paste; cut entries are dimmed, and pasting over an existing name automatically picks a unique one.
guide.assets.manage.b3: Scene files only: "Set as Startup Scene" writes the path relative to the project asset folder into startup_scene in jce_project.json, so the shipped game loads that scene on boot.
guide.assets.manage.b4: New Folder, Scene (.scene), Material (.mat.json), Physics Material (.physmat.json), Render Pipeline (.rp.json), Prefab (.prefab.json), Script (.c).
guide.assets.manage.p1: Right-click any entry to open the context menu with the common file operations; multi-select with Ctrl-click, Shift range select, or select-all.
guide.assets.manage.p2: Right-click an empty spot in the file area → Create to make common asset files directly:
guide.assets.manage.s1: Right-click an empty spot in the target folder and choose Create → New Material.
guide.assets.manage.s2: Press the rename hotkey (or right-click → Rename) to name the file; clashes with existing names get a numeric suffix automatically.
guide.assets.manage.s3: Double-click the new material to confirm its default PBR parameters in the File Viewer; it is now ready to be referenced from your scene.
guide.assets.manage.tip1: Copy / cut / paste targets flash with a highlight ring, and the results are also logged to the Console.
guide.assets.manage.title: Managing and Creating Files
guide.assets.manage.warn1: Delete is a real recursive disk delete with no recycle bin; the confirmation dialog highlights how many folders are included in the selection — read it before confirming.
guide.assets.missing.b1: Negative cache: a name that failed to resolve is not searched again for about 30 seconds (or until the index updates) — it fails instantly instead.
guide.assets.missing.b2: Budgets: a single fallback search gets at most 50 ms, and at most 3 searches run per 100 ms window — even batches of dead references cannot freeze the main thread.
guide.assets.missing.b3: Each missing material / mesh pair is warned about exactly once in the Console — no log spam.
guide.assets.missing.p1: Opening a scene with missing assets will not freeze the editor: the resolver queries the O(1) project filename index first, and only on an index miss runs a budget-limited fallback search.
guide.assets.missing.p2: To repair: resolution matches by filename across the whole project — case-insensitive, ignoring - vs _ separator differences, and stripping common asset prefixes like SM_ or T_. Putting the file back anywhere under the project root usually heals it.
guide.assets.missing.s1: Check the Console warning and note the missing filename.
guide.assets.missing.s2: Copy the file into any subfolder of the project, or fix the component's path field in the Inspector.
guide.assets.missing.s3: After about 30 seconds the negative cache expires and resolution retries automatically; reopening the project rebuilds the filename index immediately.
guide.assets.missing.tip1: Console warnings about the 50 ms search budget mean the project is large or deeply nested — keeping a clear folder structure for frequently used assets speeds up resolution noticeably.
guide.assets.missing.title: Missing-Asset Safeguards and Repair
guide.assets.missing.warn1: If multiple files share the same name, filename-based resolution may pick the wrong one — keep filenames unique within the project.
guide.assets.title: Asset Workflow
guide.assets.viewer.b1: Code / text: .c .h .cpp .lua .sc .json .toml .md and more, with syntax coloring.
guide.assets.viewer.b2: Images: .png .jpg .tga .dds .ktx2 and more, with zoom and pan.
guide.assets.viewer.b3: Models: .glb .gltf .fbx .obj, with an embedded live 3D viewport.
guide.assets.viewer.b4: Audio: .wav .ogg .mp3 and more, with waveform display and transport controls.
guide.assets.viewer.b5: Video: .mp4 .webm and more, with frame preview.
guide.assets.viewer.b6: Engine assets: Material (.mat.json), Physics Material (.physmat.json) and Render Pipeline (.rp.json) each have a dedicated viewer.
guide.assets.viewer.b7: Unrecognized binary files fall back to the hex viewer.
guide.assets.viewer.p1: The File Viewer is a multi-tab preview panel: double-click a file in the Asset Browser to open it; already-open files focus their existing tab.
guide.assets.viewer.tip1: The Physics Material and Render Pipeline viewers are directly editable; saving a render pipeline applies it to the live pipeline immediately for instant comparison.
guide.assets.viewer.tip2: The viewer is preview-first; for full code editing use the context menu "Open in VS Code".
guide.assets.viewer.title: File Viewer
guide.audio.capture.hk1: Screenshot: save the entire editor window as a PNG
guide.audio.capture.p1: The editor has built-in full-window screenshots and continuous screen recording; all encoding happens on background threads without interrupting your work, and both hotkeys stay live in Play mode.
guide.audio.capture.p2: Screenshots are written to .jce/screenshots/jce_screenshot_<timestamp>.png in your user directory, with a toast confirming the path. Capture goes through the renderer's read-back pipeline and lands on disk one frame later.
guide.audio.capture.p3: Recordings are written to .jce/recordings/rec_<timestamp>.mkv: VP9 video plus an Opus audio track (system sound via loopback capture), with the frame rate inferred from the measured gap between the first two frames.
guide.audio.capture.s1: Press the record hotkey to start; a toast shows the output file path.
guide.audio.capture.s2: Work normally or enter Play for your demo — recording keeps running.
guide.audio.capture.s3: Press it again to stop; a toast reports encoded frame and dropped frame counts.
guide.audio.capture.t1: Double-click the finished .mkv in the Asset Browser to review it in the File Viewer without leaving the editor.
guide.audio.capture.title: Screenshots & Screen Recording
guide.audio.capture.w1: System-audio loopback capture is currently Windows-only; on other platforms, or if loopback fails to initialise, the recording is video-only.
guide.audio.capture.w2: Capture queues are bounded, so frames can drop under heavy machine load; use the dropped-frame count in the stop toast to diagnose.
guide.audio.mixer.p1: The Audio Mixer manages a hierarchy of buses: Master carries four default children — Music, SFX, Voice and UI — each with its own volume, mute (M) and solo (S) switches.
guide.audio.mixer.p2: The Effective value at the end of each row is the final gain resolved along the parent chain with mute/solo applied — exactly what takes effect at runtime.
guide.audio.mixer.p3: The configuration persists to Settings/audio_mixer.json in your project. When Play starts, the runtime reads this file and mirrors every bus as a mixing group on the engine audio device; audio sources feed in via the routing rules.
guide.audio.mixer.s1: Open the Audio Mixer panel and switch to the Mixer tab.
guide.audio.mixer.s2: Click a bus name to select it; drag the slider to set volume (0–1.5), and tick M to mute or S to solo.
guide.audio.mixer.s3: Add Group creates a child bus under the selected bus; Remove deletes the selected non-Master bus.
guide.audio.mixer.s4: Volume edits are saved to disk automatically once committed; you can also press Save at any time, or Reload to return to the on-disk version.
guide.audio.mixer.t1: Bus renaming is not wired up yet (the engine mixer API does not support it), so pick good names when you create groups.
guide.audio.mixer.title: Audio Mixer
guide.audio.mixer.w1: A Play session reads the mixer configuration once at startup: changes made in the panel during Play do not affect the running session — stop and re-enter Play for them to apply.
guide.audio.reverb.b1: At runtime presets map by family: room types (Room, Bathroom, Living Room, ...) use indoor reverb, hall types (Auditorium, Concert Hall, Arena, ...) use hall reverb, cave types (Cave, Sewer Pipe, Quarry) use cave reverb, Underwater uses underwater, outdoor types (Forest, City, Mountains, ...) use outdoor; Off outputs a dry signal.
guide.audio.reverb.p1: The Audio Reverb Zone component carves out a spherical region centred on the entity's world position: full strength inside the min distance, fading out towards the max distance; when the listener (the primary camera) enters the zone, scene audio takes on the matching reverb.
guide.audio.reverb.p2: For a scene-wide overview, open the Reverb tab of the Audio Mixer panel: a table lists every zone's owner, preset and min/max distances, all editable in place.
guide.audio.reverb.s1: Select an entity and use Add Component to search for Audio Reverb Zone.
guide.audio.reverb.s2: Pick a reverb preset in the Inspector: over twenty environments such as Generic, Room, Concert Hall, Cave and Underwater.
guide.audio.reverb.s3: Adjust the min/max distances to control the full-strength radius and the width of the transition band.
guide.audio.reverb.s4: Enter Play and move the camera or character into the zone to audition the effect.
guide.audio.reverb.t1: The Ping button on each row selects the owning entity, making it easy to jump back into the scene and reposition it.
guide.audio.reverb.title: Reverb Zones
guide.audio.src.b1: Spatial Blend above 0.5 makes the source 3D: it follows the entity's world position with inverse-distance attenuation (roughly 1–25 units), and is automatically dimmed and muffled when a collider blocks the listener-to-source path.
guide.audio.src.b2: Spatial Blend at or below 0.5 keeps the source 2D — ideal for background music and UI sounds; no distance attenuation applies.
guide.audio.src.b3: Bus routing is derived by role: looping 2D sources go to the Music bus, everything else to SFX; if the project lacks the matching bus, the voice routes straight to Master.
guide.audio.src.h1: Add and configure an Audio Source
guide.audio.src.p1: Sound plays through Audio Source components attached to entities; there is no listener to place by hand — at runtime the listener automatically follows the primary camera's position and orientation, so turning the view re-spatialises the whole sound field.
guide.audio.src.s1: Select the entity that should emit sound in the Hierarchy.
guide.audio.src.s2: Click Add Component at the bottom of the Inspector, search for and pick Audio Source.
guide.audio.src.s3: Set the Audio Clip: click the field to choose from the asset picker, or drag a WAV/OGG/MP3/FLAC file from the Asset Browser straight onto the field.
guide.audio.src.s4: Tune Volume (0–1), Pitch (0.01–3) and Spatial Blend (0–1), and toggle Loop and Play On Awake as needed.
guide.audio.src.t1: Double-click an audio file in the Asset Browser to audition it in the File Viewer: play/pause, scrubbing, and a waveform display.
guide.audio.src.t2: Shipped runtimes decode Play On Awake clips asynchronously from the PAK, so the sound may start 1–2 frames after the first frame; in-editor Play uses a synchronous loader and is unaffected.
guide.audio.src.title: Audio Sources & the 3D Sound Field
guide.audio.title: Audio & Media
guide.audio.video.h1: Put a live screen in your scene
guide.audio.video.p1: The Video Player component implements video-as-texture: every frame the freshest decoded image is uploaded to a texture which the scene renderer binds as the entity mesh's albedo map — projecting video onto any model surface.
guide.audio.video.p2: Decoding capability: MP4 and WebM/MKV containers are supported; the default patent-free build decodes VP8, VP9 and AV1 video plus Opus audio tracks; H.264/H.265 video and AAC audio require the patented-codecs build switch.
guide.audio.video.p3: To confirm the codec configuration of your build, open Help → About JCE and check the Patented Codecs row.
guide.audio.video.p4: The File Viewer is a full video inspection bench: double-click a video file in the Asset Browser to open it, with play/pause (Space), rewind, timeline scrubbing, wheel zoom, drag pan, double-click fit, and a perf checkbox showing decode timing statistics.
guide.audio.video.s1: On an entity with a mesh renderer, use Add Component and pick Video Player.
guide.audio.video.s2: Set the Video Clip path (drag-and-drop from the Asset Browser works), and tick Loop and Autoplay as needed.
guide.audio.video.s3: Use the Play/Pause button in the Inspector to audition instantly; once the first frame decodes, the resolution appears next to the button.
guide.audio.video.t1: After releasing a timeline scrub, the decoder must step from the nearest keyframe to the target position; audio resume is deliberately delayed to keep A/V sync — a brief picture pause is normal.
guide.audio.video.t2: Switching to another tab automatically releases that video's decoder and texture to save memory; switching back reloads it transparently.
guide.audio.video.title: Video Playback
guide.audio.video.w1: In a patent-free build, opening an H.264/H.265 file parses metadata only and shows no picture; the viewer displays an explicit disabled-codec message — the file is not corrupt.
guide.build.bundles.b1: Open tab: pick a .jbundle or bundle_catalog.json to load the scene into the editor exactly as it would load at runtime; bundle-loaded scenes are read-only — Save is ignored.
guide.build.bundles.b2: Browse tab: after loading bundle_catalog.json you can filter by name and inspect each bundle's size, entry count, refcount, content hash and dependencies in both directions; right-click a row to copy its hash.
guide.build.bundles.hk1: Queue the current scene for single-scene packing (File > Pack Current Scene)
guide.build.bundles.p1: The Bundle Browser (Asset Pipeline workbench) is the single home for all bundle operations, with three tabs: Browse (inspect bundle_catalog.json), Build (pack scenes into .jbundle files) and Open (preview packed bundles). File > Build Bundles jumps straight to the Build tab.
guide.build.bundles.s1: On the Build tab, choose a pack mode: Project (scan every scene in the project), Selected scenes (hand-maintained list) or Single scene (one self-contained .jbundle, no catalog, no shared split).
guide.build.bundles.s2: Set up Source: in project mode fill in the project root (or click Use current); the asset root is auto-detected by default, or disable auto-detect and set it manually.
guide.build.bundles.s3: Set up Output: the output directory defaults to <project>/.bundles; non-single modes can also point at the previous catalog for incremental packing.
guide.build.bundles.s4: Expand Pack options: shared threshold (minimum 2 — assets referenced by that many scenes move into the shared bundle), shared bundle id, Zstd level 1–22, plus the Cook assets toggle and target-platform dropdown.
guide.build.bundles.s5: Click Build Bundles (shown as Pack Selected / Pack Scene depending on mode); packing runs on a worker thread, logs flow into the Console with a [bundle] prefix, and a catalog summary table appears below when done.
guide.build.bundles.t1: Scene dependency preview: with the scenes dir set, click Scan deps on a single scene file — every asset it references is listed in the Console, so you can confirm dependencies before packing.
guide.build.bundles.title: Scene bundles: packing and verification
guide.build.encryption.b1: The Bundle Browser's Build tab has its own Encrypt bundles checkbox, with the key fingerprint or a Generate button next to it; the Build Report overview counts encrypted bundles.
guide.build.encryption.p1: JCE protects embedded assets with keyed anonymous IDs, ChaCha20 payload encryption, and HMAC-SHA-256 integrity. The project key lives at <project>/.jce/pak_key.hex (32 bytes, 64 hex chars, generated by the OS CSPRNG) and Dist builds create it automatically when needed.
guide.build.encryption.s1: Open the Packaging tab of Project Settings and tick Encrypt assets; on first enable, a key is generated on the spot and its fingerprint (first 8 hex digits) is displayed.
guide.build.encryption.s2: Optionally tick Also encrypt debug builds — by default the debug variant stays plaintext, which keeps troubleshooting easy.
guide.build.encryption.s3: Manage the key with Regenerate, Show in Folder and Import; for teams or CI, use Import to distribute the same pak_key.hex to every machine.
guide.build.encryption.s4: Subsequent project builds encrypt the embedded PAK and write the key as two XOR shares into a generated jce_pak_key.c compiled into the game binary; the runtime reassembles the key before opening assets.
guide.build.encryption.t1: When a project opens, the editor installs the project key process-wide, so the editor itself can always read the project's encrypted PAKs and bundles.
guide.build.encryption.title: Asset encryption and key management
guide.build.encryption.w1: Never commit the key to version control — the editor seeds .jce/.gitignore automatically, but offline backups are on you: losing the key makes old encrypted archives permanently unreadable.
guide.build.encryption.w2: Regenerating the key makes every bundle and build encrypted with the old key unreadable (a confirmation dialog guards the action); after regenerating you must repack all bundles and rebuild everything.
guide.build.encryption.w3: Know the boundary: archive integrity is authenticated, but the key necessarily ships inside the game binary. Protection raises extraction cost; it is not secrecy, so do not ship genuinely sensitive data in the client.
guide.build.pipeline.b1: The Stop button is enabled while a build is running and requests cancellation of the current build.
guide.build.pipeline.b2: The Pack Game button builds, verifies and stages: it copies the executable and cooked assets into build/<platform>-<arch>/dist/<name>-<version>-<platform>-<arch>/.
guide.build.pipeline.p1: The Play button drives a three-stage state machine: Cook (asset cooking, skipped when nothing changed), then Build (compile), then on success it launches the game executable automatically. Every stage logs into the Console.
guide.build.pipeline.s1: Open the Build Profiles panel and select a profile in the left list.
guide.build.pipeline.s2: Check the state of the Cook before build checkbox (on by default; the Cook stage is skipped when assets are already up to date).
guide.build.pipeline.s3: Click Play. The status text walks through cooking, building and running; the status line also reports the stage (configure, compile, conan install, cooking assets) and the result (succeeded, failed).
guide.build.pipeline.s4: Follow the [build] log in the Console; once the game starts, its stdout/stderr flows back into the Console with a [run] prefix, and the process exit code is printed too.
guide.build.pipeline.t1: Closing the panel does not interrupt the pipeline — the underlying managers keep running in the background, and progress resumes the next time the panel opens.
guide.build.pipeline.title: One-click pipeline: Cook → Build → Run
guide.build.pipeline.w1: If cmake, ninja or conan is missing, the Play and Build Project buttons are disabled; check the tool status strip and install the missing tool first.
guide.build.platforms.b1: Architecture: the arch dropdown in Build Profiles (project mode) offers host, x86_64, i686, aarch64 and armv7; with host selected, the build system probes the local machine.
guide.build.platforms.b2: Texture format follows the target platform: in the bundle cook target dropdown, Windows/Linux/macOS use BC compression while Android/iOS/Web use ASTC — switch it when shipping to mobile or Web, or the target GPU cannot use the textures.
guide.build.platforms.b3: The --dist checkbox only appears on Windows; the dist variant and the Web platform force patented codecs (AAC/H.264/H.265) off at the build-system level, keeping royalty-free formats only.
guide.build.platforms.b4: Pack Game output path template: <project>/build/<win32|linux|darwin>-<arch>/dist/<name>-<version>-<platform>-<arch>/ — one directory is one distributable copy.
guide.build.platforms.p1: One project can target Windows, Linux and macOS desktops plus Android, iOS and Web; the differences concentrate in three places: texture cook format, patented codecs and output directory layout.
guide.build.platforms.t1: Command line and CI: the authoritative build entry for the engine workspace is scripts/jce.py; the editor panel delegates to the platform build scripts in engine-workspace mode and drives cmake/ninja natively in user-project mode — the artifact layout stays the same.
guide.build.platforms.title: Multi-platform notes
guide.build.platforms.w1: Assets that depend on patented codecs such as AAC or H.264 will fail to decode in dist and Web builds — replace them with royalty-free source assets before shipping.
guide.build.profiles.b1: Project root: type a path or click Browse…; picking a file such as CMakePresets.json or jce_project.json is fine — it is normalized to its parent directory and persisted in the editor config.
guide.build.profiles.b2: Tool status strip: the panel probes cmake, conan and ninja; if any shows [MISSING], the build buttons are disabled. Hover a badge for its version, click Recheck to probe again.
guide.build.profiles.b3: Options: --clean for a full rebuild; --dist for the distribution variant (checkbox shown on Windows only); Target and Exe set the CMake target and output filename (pre-filled when the project has jce_project.json); project mode adds an arch dropdown: host, x86_64, i686, aarch64, armv7.
guide.build.profiles.b4: User-project mode needs an SDK: enter the SDK directory in SDK Root (click Save SDK to write it into jce_project.json's sdk_path), or set the JCE_SDK_DIR environment variable. This mode drives cmake/ninja natively, with no scripts involved.
guide.build.profiles.hk1: Open Build Profiles (File > Build Settings points at the same panel)
guide.build.profiles.p1: The Build Profiles panel is the single surface for build configuration and triggering: in engine-workspace mode it lists every configurePreset from CMakePresets.json; in user-project mode (jce_project.json detected) it synthesizes one project profile. Builds run asynchronously on a background thread and logs stream into the Console with a [build] prefix, so the editor never blocks.
guide.build.profiles.p2: After a successful build, with the auto-update checkbox enabled (default), the panel rewrites the game executable path and working directory in the editor config and switches to the Build Report tab.
guide.build.profiles.t1: Once a profile is selected on the left, the detail pane shows the predicted output path plus the Conan profile and output folder derived from CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE — you can confirm where artifacts will land before building.
guide.build.profiles.title: Build Profiles panel: presets and options
guide.build.report.b1: The Duplicates tab clusters assets by content hash and lists those copied into multiple bundles — the number-one source of wasted size; raising the shared threshold moves them into the shared bundle.
guide.build.report.p1: The Build Report is the second tab of the Build Profiles workbench. It reads build_report.json (schema jce.buildreport.v1), which the bundle packer emits next to bundle_catalog.json. The panel is read-only; a background packer may rewrite the file at any time.
guide.build.report.s1: The report path defaults to <project>/bundles/build_report.json; you can point it at any report file.
guide.build.report.s2: Click Load to read the report; the status line shows the bundle count and total size.
guide.build.report.s3: Switch between the five tabs: Overview (timestamp, total size, unique assets, duplicate clusters, encrypted-bundle count), Bundles, Entries, Duplicates and Top-N.
guide.build.report.s4: Use the filter box to narrow by name or path; on the Top-N tab, drag the slider (1–200) to find the largest asset entries, with bars for visual size comparison.
guide.build.report.t1: Engine-workspace builds also run tools/gen_pak_report.py automatically, generating a self-contained HTML report (e.g. game_assets_report.html) under reports/ in the build tree — open it in a browser to inspect compression ratios and size composition (requires Python3).
guide.build.report.t2: The panel switches to this tab automatically after a successful build; the manual entry lives under Window > Workbenches > Build Profiles > Build Report.
guide.build.report.title: Build Report: size and duplicate analysis
guide.build.title: Build & Distribution
guide.diag.layout.b1: Default: Unity-style three columns, Hierarchy on the left, Scene/Game views in the center, Inspector on the right, Asset Browser and Console at the bottom.
guide.diag.layout.b10: Lighting: Scene view in the center, the Lighting Settings workbench on the right, Hierarchy on the left, Console below, ideal for lighting iteration.
guide.diag.layout.b2: Wide: drops the left-column squeeze, widens the Inspector to about 35% and shrinks the bottom strip, made for ultra-wide displays.
guide.diag.layout.b3: Animation: the bottom 40% goes to the Animation Editor and Timeline, with Scene and Inspector above.
guide.diag.layout.b4: Two by Two: a four-pane grid, Scene and Game views on top, Hierarchy/Assets and Console/Inspector below, good for side-by-side comparison debugging.
guide.diag.layout.b5: Programmer: nearly half the screen at the bottom for Console and Asset Browser, de-emphasizing the Game view to focus on logs and diagnostics.
guide.diag.layout.b6: 2D: a large central canvas with a 30% bottom strip of Assets/Console, prepared for sprite and tilemap workflows.
guide.diag.layout.b7: Mobile Portrait: deliberately narrows the central viewport to mimic a portrait phone's aspect ratio, giving the sides to Hierarchy and Inspector.
guide.diag.layout.b8: Cinematic: Scene view dominant, VCam Manager on the right, Timeline at the bottom, serving camera work and cutscene production.
guide.diag.layout.b9: Profiling: the performance tools (Profiling workbench, Network Stats, Physics Debugger) clustered as upper-left tabs, Game view on the right, Console at the bottom.
guide.diag.layout.p1: Layout presets rearrange every docked panel in one click; the current layout persists in .jce/imgui.ini and survives editor restarts. There are 10 presets:
guide.diag.layout.p2: Workspaces are a Maya-style layer above presets: the workspace dropdown at the right of the menu bar and Ctrl+F1 through Ctrl+F7 switch between the seven workspaces Default/Modeling/Rigging/Animation/FX/Rendering/UV Editing; the eighth, Sculpting, is unbound by default. Switching a workspace applies its layout preset and makes its key panels visible, and the active workspace is remembered across sessions.
guide.diag.layout.s1: Open Window - Layout Presets and pick a preset; every panel rearranges to it immediately.
guide.diag.layout.s2: Drag any panel by its title to dock it elsewhere; your customization is remembered automatically.
guide.diag.layout.s3: If the layout gets messy, run Window - Reset Layout to return to the default preset.
guide.diag.layout.tip1: Newly enabled panels never float loose: a panel with no saved position docks automatically as a tab next to its most natural sibling (World Streaming next to Navmesh, for example), falling back to Console/Inspector when no sibling is alive.
guide.diag.layout.title: Layouts & Workspaces
guide.diag.prefs.b1: General: autosave interval (off/1/5/15 minutes), startup behavior (restore last project / empty scene / project picker), recent-project count (1 to 20).
guide.diag.prefs.b2: Appearance: UI language (lists every installed language pack, switches instantly on selection), theme (Dark/Light/Blue), font size (12 to 32, live preview while dragging, re-baked on release), UI scale (0.5 to 3.0x), and the renderer backend selection.
guide.diag.prefs.b3: Fonts: pick separate fonts for Latin and CJK text from a scan of system fonts; leave on Auto to use the built-in selection strategy.
guide.diag.prefs.b4: Viewport: scene grid visibility, view mode (shaded/wireframe/textured), default Asset Browser view (grid/details).
guide.diag.prefs.b5: Input: invert scroll-wheel zoom, invert drag Y axis, invert horizontal touchpad scrolling.
guide.diag.prefs.b6: Paths: build output directory, auto-repack-on-save toggle, run the game in developer mode.
guide.diag.prefs.b7: Hotkeys: a rebinding table for every editor shortcut, with filtering, Bind-then-press capture, per-row or global reset to defaults; bindings that conflict with another action are marked red with the conflicting action named.
guide.diag.prefs.b8: Toolchains: shows the detected status and version of CMake, Ninja, MSVC, GCC, Clang, Android NDK, Emscripten SDK and Xcode on this machine, with manual path overrides when auto-detection picks wrong.
guide.diag.prefs.p1: Preferences is a modal window for user-level settings with eight pages on the left. Most changes apply instantly and persist automatically to prefs.json, editor-config.json and hotkeys.json under the per-user .jce directory, shared across projects.
guide.diag.prefs.s1: Open the window via Edit - Preferences (or the hotkey above).
guide.diag.prefs.s2: Switch to the Hotkeys page, filter for the target action, click Bind and press the new chord (Esc cancels capture).
guide.diag.prefs.s3: Just close the window: changes are written to disk the moment you make them, there is no separate save button.
guide.diag.prefs.tip1: UI language switching is instant and this guide's text follows along; four language packs (English / Simplified Chinese / Japanese / Korean) ship with the editor.
guide.diag.prefs.title: Preferences
guide.diag.prefs.warn1: A renderer backend change only takes effect on the next editor launch; everything else applies immediately.
guide.diag.profiler.b1: CPU tab: frame-time graph with an FPS status chip (green at 55+, yellow at 30+, red below 30), a stacked frame-budget bar (CPU/GPU/wait), the bgfx renderer resource table (draw calls, textures, shaders, VRAM and more), plus scene culling, LOD, render-queue batching, occlusion culling, world streaming, process memory and a sortable per-view hotspot table.
guide.diag.profiler.b2: Memory tab: process RSS/commit and mimalloc reserved/committed up top; a total-usage bar against a 512 MB baseline in the middle; below, a per-tag table of current/peak/live count/lifetime totals (sortable headers, rows turn red when a single tag exceeds 64 MB). Refresh rate is selectable: 0.1/0.5/1/5 seconds.
guide.diag.profiler.b3: Profile Analyzer tab: a rolling record of the last 256 frames of frame/CPU/GPU/wait times; frames above the spike threshold (default 33.3 ms) are highlighted red and listed in a spike table. Supports pausing capture, clearing, and exporting profile_export.csv.
guide.diag.profiler.b4: Frame Debugger tab: bgfx per-frame totals (draw/compute/blit counts, CPU and GPU times, wait times, backbuffer and resource counts), the per-view GPU/CPU timing table, plus the render-queue submission breakdown (commands to actual submits, instanced batches and total instances) and per-level LOD pick counts.
guide.diag.profiler.p1: The Profiling workbench gathers four diagnostic tools as tabs of a single window: CPU, Memory, Profile Analyzer and Frame Debugger. Data comes straight from bgfx frame stats, the scene renderer's per-frame counters and the engine's memory-tag statistics, with no external capture tool required, so it works in release editor builds too.
guide.diag.profiler.s1: Open the workbench via Window - Workbenches - Profiler (or the hotkey above).
guide.diag.profiler.s2: Stay on the CPU tab and read the FPS chip and frame-budget bars to decide whether the bottleneck is CPU, GPU or synchronization waits.
guide.diag.profiler.s3: Click the copy button at the top right to put a full text snapshot (frame stats, renderer, culling, streaming, process memory) on the clipboard, handy for tickets or before/after comparisons.
guide.diag.profiler.s4: Switch to the Memory tab: click Reset Peaks first, perform the operation you are investigating, then click Snapshot to write a timestamped mem_snapshot_*.json for the record.
guide.diag.profiler.tip1: Click the headers of the view hotspot table to change the sort column and direction; the same table is reused by the Frame Debugger tab and self-refreshes every frame even when the CPU tab is not active.
guide.diag.profiler.title: Profiling Workbench
guide.diag.profiler.warn1: The CPU tab's history curves are only sampled while that tab is in the foreground, with a window of about 240 frames (roughly 4 seconds at 60 FPS); after switching away and back, or clicking Reset History, the curves accumulate from scratch.
guide.diag.project.b1: The Input page embeds the full Input Manager (action and binding editing) plus global parameters such as treat-keyboard-as-dpad, gamepad enable, stick dead zone, recentering gravity and sensitivity.
guide.diag.project.b2: The Physics page includes a 32-layer collision matrix: tick which layer pairs collide, with layer names shared with the Tags & Layers page.
guide.diag.project.b3: The Localization page is the game string-table grid (key by locale): add keys and locales, edit each locale's text in place; the preview-locale dropdown instantly drives UIText in the game view and Play sessions; the grid has its own Save button below, writing back to i18n/<locale>.json in the source assets directory.
guide.diag.project.p1: Project Settings is the project-level configuration hub: a modal window with a filterable page list on the left, 17 pages in total covering Project, Build, Run, Hotkeys, Input, Physics, Physics 2D, Tags & Layers, Quality, Graphics, Time, Player, Packaging, Preset Manager, Audio, Editor and Localization. Saving writes the project settings file and applies it to the engine immediately.
guide.diag.project.s1: Open the window via File - Project Settings (or the hotkey above).
guide.diag.project.s2: Type a keyword into the top-left filter box to jump to the page you need.
guide.diag.project.s3: After editing, an unsaved marker appears at the bottom; click Save to write and apply, or Revert to discard all unsaved changes.
guide.diag.project.tip1: Keys marked with an [L] lock in the localization grid are consumed by the engine's built-in pause/settings menu: their text can be edited but the keys themselves cannot be deleted.
guide.diag.project.title: Project Settings
guide.diag.project.warn1: Unlike Preferences, changes in this panel only hit disk when you click the Save button at the bottom; the localization grid has its own separate Save button and unsaved indicator, so do not miss it.
guide.diag.tests.p1: The Test Runner scans a configurable directory (default scripts/tests) for *.test.json manifests. Each manifest describes one test suite: suite is the suite name, exe points at the executable to run, and the cases array lists case names with their command-line arguments.
guide.diag.tests.p2: When running, the panel launches the executable once per case and captures combined stdout and stderr; exit code 0 is recorded as PASS, anything else as FAIL. The left tree shows suites, cases, status and duration; the right side shows total/pass/fail counts and the full output of the selected case.
guide.diag.tests.s1: Create xxx.test.json under the project's scripts/tests directory and fill in the suite, exe and cases fields (exe points at a test executable the repo already builds).
guide.diag.tests.s2: Open the panel, make sure the directory box at the top points at the manifest directory, then click Rescan to load the suites.
guide.diag.tests.s3: Click Run All, or the Run button on a suite row; the status column turns PASS/FAIL with the duration.
guide.diag.tests.s4: Select a failed case and read its stdout/stderr in the output pane on the right to pinpoint the failure.
guide.diag.tests.tip1: The engine does not impose a test framework: any executable that reports success via its exit code (catch2, unity-test, hand-rolled smoke exes) can be hooked into a manifest directly.
guide.diag.tests.title: Test Runner
guide.diag.tests.warn1: Cases run synchronously: the editor UI freezes until the case exits. Split long tests into small cases, or run them in external CI.
guide.diag.title: Diagnostics & Customization
guide.diag.vcs.p1: The Version Control panel is a read-only Git status view: it runs git in the project root to query the current branch and working-tree state, rendering the result as a status/path table with the branch name on top.
guide.diag.vcs.s1: Open the panel; the first time it appears it automatically queries the current branch and status once.
guide.diag.vcs.s2: After editing scenes or assets, click Refresh to re-read the working-tree changes.
guide.diag.vcs.s3: Check the change set against the Modified/Added/Deleted/Renamed/Untracked labels, then commit in your Git client of choice.
guide.diag.vcs.tip1: The panel needs an open project root and git on the system PATH; if the directory is not a Git repository it shows a notice instead of erroring out.
guide.diag.vcs.title: Version Control
guide.diag.vcs.warn1: The panel is currently read-only: staging, committing, diffing and pushing are not wired into the editor yet, so use the command line or an external Git tool.
guide.hotkeys.intro: This table is generated live from the hotkey registry — if you rebound keys in Preferences > Hotkeys, the chords shown here are the ones currently in effect.
guide.hotkeys.rebind: Rebinding: open Edit > Preferences > Hotkeys, click any row and press a new chord; conflicts are flagged immediately.
guide.hotkeys.title: Hotkey Reference
guide.inspector.addcomp.p1: The Add Component button at the bottom of the Inspector opens a searchable list covering every attachable component — rendering, physics, audio, animation, UI, networking and more; components already on the entity are hidden from the list.
guide.inspector.addcomp.p2: A new component is initialized with its registry defaults and inserted into the component list in default order.
guide.inspector.addcomp.p3: Every component header has an enable checkbox right after its name, so you can switch a single component off without removing it; a disabled section is dimmed but its fields stay visible. Transform is essential — always enabled and not removable.
guide.inspector.addcomp.p4: The "..." button on the right of a component header opens the component menu: Copy Component, Paste Component Values, Move Up/Down, Preset, Reset, and the red Remove Component at the bottom.
guide.inspector.addcomp.p5: Copy Component stores the component's full values in the component clipboard; switch to the same component type on another entity and choose Paste Component Values from its "..." menu to overwrite it.
guide.inspector.addcomp.s1: Select an entity and click the Add Component button at the bottom of the Inspector.
guide.inspector.addcomp.s2: Type into the search field to filter; the search matches both the English name and the translated names of every UI language.
guide.inspector.addcomp.s3: Click a list entry to add it; you can also press Enter to add the first match, or Esc to close the popup.
guide.inspector.addcomp.tip1: Drag a component header to reorder components in the Inspector — equivalent to Move Up/Down in the menu; the order only affects display, not runtime logic.
guide.inspector.addcomp.tip2: Every field edit in the Inspector goes into the undo history, so feel free to experiment.
guide.inspector.addcomp.title: Adding & Managing Components
guide.inspector.addcomp.warn1: Paste Component Values is only available when the target component matches the clipboard's component type exactly; the clipboard holds one component value at a time.
guide.inspector.addcomp.warn2: Reset restores the component to its defaults (Transform resets to the origin with unit scale); the operation is undoable too.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b1: Animator — a simple clip player: clip name, speed, loop and a play button (currently badged "not simulated").
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b10: UI Image / UI Text / UI Button — the basic UI widgets: image, text and button.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b11: Network Object — the network identity, prerequisite for replication; net_id is assigned by the server at spawn and shown read-only.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b12: Network Transform / Network Animator / Network Rigidbody — replicate transform, animation and rigid body respectively (the latter two currently badged "not simulated").
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b13: Script — attaches a script file (currently badged "not simulated").
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b14: Behavior Tree — references a behavior-tree XML asset, loaded at Play and ticked every frame; watch it live in the BT Visualizer panel.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b15: Nav Agent — a navigation agent: radius, height, max speed/acceleration and other pathfinding parameters, used with navmeshes baked in the NavMesh workbench.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b16: Spawn Manager — spawn manager: pedestrian/vehicle caps and spawn radius range.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b17: Weapon — a weapon: hitscan or projectile kind, plus damage, range and related parameters.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b18: Save Point — a save point: save ID, display name, manual/auto/checkpoint kind and trigger radius.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b19: Pivot — a Maya-style pivot: gives the entity its own manipulator pivot point and orientation.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b2: Skeletal Animator — skeletal animation: skeleton/model asset, clip list, speed, loop, blend tree, plus an optional animation state machine asset; once set, parameters drive the active clip.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b20: Transform — every entity's base position, rotation and scale, with parent/child hierarchy.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b21: Foot IK — ground-adaptive foot placement: raycasts under each foot and bends the legs while the hips drop to the lowest foot.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b22: Full-Body IK — coordinated multi-effector IK: each effector pulls a named bone toward a world target while bone lengths stay rigid, propagating through the shared spine.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b23: Morph Weights — drives blendshape (morph target) weights for facial expressions and mesh deformation.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b24: Gameplay Ability System — abilities, attributes and gameplay tags, with attribute replication.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b25: Network Variable — a replicated variable (float/int) with an on-value-changed hook and late-join baseline.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b4: IK Constraints — IK constraints; the full constraint stack is authored in the Animation workbench's Rigging tab, with a shortcut button in the section.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b5: Avatar — avatar/skeleton-mapping asset, mask and root-motion toggle (currently badged "not simulated").
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b6: Sequence Player — references and plays a Sequencer sequence asset.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b7: Canvas — the UI canvas, container for UI widgets.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b8: Canvas Group — controls opacity and interactivity of child UI as a group.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.b9: Layout Group — arranges child UI elements automatically.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.p1: This section covers animation, UI, networking and gameplay-logic components.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.tip1: When you add a Net sync component such as Network Transform, the editor automatically attaches a Network Object as well, so the sync data is not skipped at runtime.
guide.inspector.comps_logic.title: Component Catalog: Animation, UI, Networking & Logic
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b1: Rigidbody — a rigid body: mass, friction, restitution, drag/angular drag, gravity toggle and scale, kinematic mode, CCD, physics layer and physics material.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b10: Cloth — cloth simulation; parameter changes rebuild the runtime cloth automatically.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b11: Trigger Volume — a trigger volume: AABB/sphere/OBB shapes, with a tag field and an option to fire stay events continuously.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b12: Rigidbody 2D / Collider 2D / Joint 2D — the 2D physics trio.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b13: Tilemap Collider 2D — auto-generates 2D collision from a tile map.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b14: Audio Source — an audio source: clip, volume, pitch, 2D/3D spatial blend, loop and play-on-awake.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b15: Audio Listener — the listener, usually on the camera or player entity.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b16: Audio Reverb Zone — a reverb zone.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b18: Vehicle — full vehicle physics: a chassis driven through Wheel Colliders with throttle, steering and brakes.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b19: Soft Body — a volumetric (pressure) soft body; its centroid is published back to the entity.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b2: Box / Sphere / Capsule Collider — the three primitive colliders, each with center offset and size parameters; all can act as triggers.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b20: Buoyancy — applies buoyant lift by sampling water-surface depth so the body floats.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b21: Ragdoll — a physics ragdoll built at Play from the skeleton; blend by weight for death/hit reactions.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b22: Fracture — breakable geometry: on impact the body shatters into Voronoi convex-hull fragments.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b3: Mesh Collider — a mesh-shaped collider with an optional convex mode.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b4: Compound Collider — a compound collider auto-generated from a model, with V-HACD convex-decomposition parameters.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b7: Constraint — a basic physics constraint: type, target entity, pivots on both sides, axis and limits.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.b9: Constant Force — a continuously applied force.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.p1: This section covers physics and audio components. 3D physics is built on Bullet, 2D physics on Box2D.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.tip1: The Scene view draws wireframe outlines for colliders, so you can check centers and sizes against the model while tuning.
guide.inspector.comps_physics.title: Component Catalog: Physics & Audio
guide.inspector.comps_physics.warn1: Wheel Collider, Constant Force, Configurable Joint and Joint 2D currently carry the "not simulated" badge: their parameters can be authored and saved with the scene but have no runtime effect yet.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b1: Mesh Renderer — renders a 3D model or built-in shape with a full PBR material: base color, metallic, roughness, emissive, texture maps, alpha mode and shadow cast/receive toggles.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b10: Tilemap — a 2D tile map, painted in the Tile Palette.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b12: Light — light sources; directional, point and spot lights are unified into a single Light section in the Inspector.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b13: Reflection Probe — provides local reflections for nearby objects.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b14: Light Probe Group — a group of light probes.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b15: Volume — a box/sphere post-processing volume that overrides exposure, gamma, bloom, vignette, chromatic aberration and more per region, with blend distance, weight and a global mode.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b16: Occlusion Portal — an occlusion-culling portal: size, open/closed state and portal ID.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b17: Camera — a rendering camera: field of view, near/far planes, orthographic projection, primary-camera flag and clear mode.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b18: Virtual Camera — a virtual camera, orchestrated with the Virtual Camera Manager.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b19: Video Player — plays a video file by path, with loop and autoplay options.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b2: Sprite Renderer — renders a 2D sprite with tinting, horizontal/vertical flips and a sorting order.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b20: Water — an animated water surface with waves; also a buoyancy depth source for floating bodies.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b21: Vegetation Scatter — instanced grass/tree scattering across terrain or a mesh.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b3: Billboard Renderer — a quad that always faces the camera.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b4: Trail Renderer — generates a trail as the entity moves.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b5: Line Renderer — renders line segments and polylines.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b6: Decal Projector — projects a decal onto scene surfaces.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b7: Particle Emitter — particle effects such as fire and dust.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b8: LOD Group — switches detail levels by camera distance.
guide.inspector.comps_render.b9: Terrain — terrain component, edited together with the Terrain panel.
guide.inspector.comps_render.p1: All of the following components can be attached via Add Component. This section covers rendering and environment components, one line each.
guide.inspector.comps_render.title: Component Catalog: Rendering, Cameras & Environment
guide.inspector.comps_render.warn1: Some component sections carry a yellow "not simulated" badge (here: Trail/Line/Billboard Renderer and Occlusion Portal): the data is saved with the scene, but the engine runtime does not consume it yet, so it has no effect in Play mode or shipped games.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b1: Canvas — the UI root (Screen-Space Overlay) with a reference resolution and scale mode.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b10: UI Scroll View — a clipped, scrollable container for content larger than its viewport.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b11: UI Dropdown — an expandable option selector; fires on-value-changed.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b12: UI Progress Bar — a read-only fill bar driven by gameplay/scripts.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b2: Canvas Group — group alpha, interactable and block-raycasts for all child UI.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b3: Layout Group — auto-arranges child elements horizontally, vertically or in a grid.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b4: UI Image — a textured/colored quad with nine-slice and fill modes.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b5: UI Text — a localized text label with font and alignment.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b6: UI Button — hover/press tinting plus an on-click handler dispatched to a script.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b7: UI Slider — a draggable value in a range; fires on-value-changed.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b8: UI Toggle — an on/off checkbox; fires on-value-changed.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.b9: UI Input Field — single-line text entry with content-type filtering; fires on-value-changed and on-submit.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.p1: The UI components build a runtime Canvas. Containers lay out widgets; widgets are interactive and dispatch their events to gameplay scripts.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.tip1: Slider, Toggle, Input Field, Dropdown and Button dispatch their value/submit events to gameplay scripts; Progress Bar is display-only.
guide.inspector.comps_ui.title: Component Catalog: UI Controls
guide.inspector.multiselect.hk1: Select all entities in the scene
guide.inspector.multiselect.p1: In the Hierarchy, Ctrl+click adds or removes individual entities from the selection and Shift+click selects a range; with multiple entities selected, the Inspector shows the multi-select view on top while the focused entity's component sections remain below.
guide.inspector.multiselect.p2: The multi-select view offers shared controls: the Enabled checkbox toggles all selected entities at once; with mixed states it switches to Enable All / Disable All buttons; when every entity shares the same tag color you can recolor them together.
guide.inspector.multiselect.p3: Inside the Transform (Bulk) section: position is a relative offset (cleared after applying), rotation and scale are absolute, and scale offers a uniform checkbox; each row takes effect via its Apply button, with one-click position/scale resets. A whole bulk apply collapses into a single undo entry.
guide.inspector.multiselect.p4: Below, the selected entities are listed (up to 20 shown): clicking a name switches the focused preview within the selection; the crosshair icon collapses the selection to that single entity and frames the camera on it; the X icon removes the entity from the selection.
guide.inspector.multiselect.p5: While multi-selecting, edits made in the focused entity's component sections are broadcast per field to the other selected entities holding the same component: only the field you just changed is copied, every other field keeps its per-entity value.
guide.inspector.multiselect.p6: Field broadcasting only applies to a whitelist of pure value-type components: Transform, Mesh Renderer, Camera, Sprite Renderer, Skeletal Animator, Constraint, Rigidbody, Box/Sphere/Capsule/Mesh/Compound Collider and Audio Source.
guide.inspector.multiselect.s1: Ctrl+click in the Hierarchy to select several entities that carry a Rigidbody.
guide.inspector.multiselect.s2: Drag Mass in the focused entity's Rigidbody section and watch the other selected entities update to the same value.
guide.inspector.multiselect.s3: To clear them out, click the red Delete Selected button at the bottom to delete all selected entities at once (a confirmation dialog appears first).
guide.inspector.multiselect.title: Multi-Select & Bulk Editing
guide.inspector.multiselect.warn1: Components outside the whitelist do not participate in broadcasting (especially those with string or asset-path fields) and must be edited per entity.
guide.inspector.overview.p1: The Inspector shows every property of the focused entity: a header area at the top (name, enable toggle, tag color, tag and layer) followed by the entity's component sections in order. Click an entity in the Hierarchy to focus it in the Inspector.
guide.inspector.overview.s1: Click an entity in the Hierarchy; the Inspector immediately shows its properties.
guide.inspector.overview.s2: Edit the entity name in the top input field and press Enter to commit.
guide.inspector.overview.s3: Use the Enabled checkbox below the name to switch the whole entity on or off; a disabled entity no longer takes effect in the scene and its component sections become read-only.
guide.inspector.overview.s4: Use the Tag Color dropdown to color-code the entity (easy to spot in the Hierarchy); type a tag in the Tag field and press Enter — new tags are registered into the project settings automatically; the arrow button next to the field picks from existing tags.
guide.inspector.overview.s5: Pick the entity's layer from the Layer dropdown; only named layers are listed, and layer names are managed in the Tags & Layers panel.
guide.inspector.overview.tip1: The red Delete button next to the name asks for confirmation before deleting the entity; the delete hotkey below works on the current selection as well.
guide.inspector.overview.title: Inspector Overview
guide.inspector.overview.warn1: In Play mode an orange warning appears at the top of the Inspector: any edits made to entities will be reverted when playback stops.
guide.inspector.presets.p1: A preset saves a component's complete values as a named file under the project's presets/<ComponentName>/ directory, ready to re-apply across entities and scenes — ideal for recurring material parameters, rigid-body setups and the like.
guide.inspector.presets.p2: Presets are filed per component type, so each component's preset list stays separate; presets are plain project files and can be version-controlled and shared with the team.
guide.inspector.presets.s1: After tuning the component, click the "..." on its header and expand the Preset submenu.
guide.inspector.presets.s2: Choose "Save As Preset…", type a name and click Save (or just press Enter).
guide.inspector.presets.s3: Make sure the target entity carries the same component, open the Preset submenu again, expand the preset name and click Apply.
guide.inspector.presets.s4: Delete an obsolete preset via the red Delete entry in its submenu.
guide.inspector.presets.tip1: Applying a preset goes into the undo history — just undo if you applied the wrong one.
guide.inspector.presets.title: Component Presets
guide.inspector.presets.warn1: A preset can only be applied onto an existing component of the same type — add the component first; after engine upgrades that change a component's layout, old presets may refuse to load due to a size mismatch.
guide.inspector.title: Inspector & Components
guide.physics.bodies.b1: Body type is derived from the fields: Is Kinematic checked makes it Kinematic; mass 0 makes it Static; otherwise it is Dynamic.
guide.physics.bodies.b2: Collider shape components: Box (center + size), Sphere (center + radius), Capsule (center + radius + height), Mesh Collider (convex hull or triangle mesh from a model asset), and Compound Collider (auto-fitted box/sphere/capsule/convex hull per model part, with VHACD convex decomposition and triangle-mesh modes). All sizes are multiplied by the entity scale.
guide.physics.bodies.b3: An entity with only a Rigidbody and no collider gets a placeholder box from its transform scale at runtime, so dropped objects still collide.
guide.physics.bodies.b4: Priority on a single entity: Character Controller > Compound Collider > Mesh Collider > Rigidbody with primitive shapes; if Compound and Mesh coexist, Compound wins and a warning is logged.
guide.physics.bodies.p1: The Rigidbody component provides mass, drag/angular drag, Use Gravity with Gravity Scale, a kinematic toggle, friction and restitution, a collision layer, a physics-material reference, and CCD (continuous collision detection) settings. Once a physics material is assigned, the inline friction and restitution are disabled and the material wins.
guide.physics.bodies.p2: Physics materials: right-click empty space in the Asset Browser to create a .physmat.json; double-click to edit static/dynamic friction, restitution and the two combine modes in the File Viewer, then drag the file onto the Physics Material slot of a Rigidbody or Compound Collider.
guide.physics.bodies.p3: The Constraint component (point-to-point / hinge / slider / 6DoF) works in Play: drag another entity from the Hierarchy into the Connected Body slot, or leave it empty to anchor to the world; hinge and slider also expose an axis and lower/upper limits. Constraints are created together after all bodies have spawned.
guide.physics.bodies.s1: Create a cube from the menu (GameObject → 3D Object → Cube).
guide.physics.bodies.s2: In the Inspector, click Add Component, then search for and add Rigidbody and Box Collider.
guide.physics.bodies.s3: Set mass above 0, lift the cube off the ground, and enter Play to watch it fall and collide.
guide.physics.bodies.t1: When fast small objects tunnel through thin walls, set the CCD mode to Continuous or Continuous Dynamic; choosing a non-Discrete mode reveals motion-threshold and swept-sphere-radius controls.
guide.physics.bodies.title: Rigid Bodies & Colliders
guide.physics.bodies.w1: The Capsule Collider axis dropdown (X/Y/Z) only affects the editor preview; at runtime the capsule is fixed to the Y axis, matching the scene-view overlay wireframe.
guide.physics.bodies.w2: Wheel Collider, Constant Force, Configurable Joint and Joint 2D carry a yellow 'not simulated' badge at the top of their panels: their values are saved with the scene but the engine runtime does not consume them yet.
guide.physics.character.b1: Capsule fields: height, radius, step offset, slope limit; values left at 0 fall back to engine defaults 1.8 / 0.35 / 0.35 / 50°.
guide.physics.character.b2: Feel fields: move speed (default 4), sprint multiplier (1.8), jump speed (5), acceleration, air control, turn speed (720°/s).
guide.physics.character.b3: Built-in 0.12 s coyote time and 0.12 s jump buffer: you can still jump right after walking off a ledge, and an early jump press fires the moment you land; releasing the jump key mid-rise cuts the ascent for controllable jump height.
guide.physics.character.b4: The entity Transform represents the feet; the runtime automatically raises the capsule center by half the height, so simply place the character on the ground — it will neither sink nor float.
guide.physics.character.p1: The Character Controller is a velocity-driven dynamic capsule rigid body (rotation locked), not a traditional kinematic controller, so it interacts naturally with pushable crates and other dynamic objects. Grounding uses a 5-ray fan probe, with step height (Step Offset) and slope limit support.
guide.physics.character.s1: Add a Character Controller component to the character entity and fit the capsule height and radius to the model.
guide.physics.character.s2: Enter Play and focus the Game view; drive the character with the Input Manager actions move_forward / move_back / move_left / move_right, jump, and sprint — missing actions fall back to WASD and Space.
guide.physics.character.s3: Open the Physics Debugger and enable Wireframe to watch the capsule's ground contact during Play.
guide.physics.character.t1: Input only provides a camera-relative unit direction; actual speed is decided entirely by the component fields. Air control has a minimum of 0.01 — the engine treats 0 as 'use the default 0.35'.
guide.physics.character.title: Character Controller
guide.physics.character.w1: Only one Character Controller is supported per scene (the first spawned entity wins); a Rigidbody on the same entity is skipped.
guide.physics.debug.b1: The debug-draw switches (wireframe / AABB / contacts / constraints / normals) read directly from the Bullet world, so they only show during a Play session.
guide.physics.debug.b2: Joint Gizmos and Cloth Gizmos are separate toggles: joints draw for the selected entities, cloth reads the live solver vertices.
guide.physics.debug.b3: Runtime Stats shows total bodies and active contacts (requires a Play session); sleeping bodies and query counts are placeholders for now.
guide.physics.debug.b4: The 3D / 2D layer matrices in this panel are the same data as the Project Settings Physics page; checkbox changes are saved immediately.
guide.physics.debug.hk2: Step one frame (1/60 s) while paused
guide.physics.debug.p1: Click View in the Scene view toolbar and check Physics Debug (wireframe) to show collider wireframes for the whole scene: boxes are green, spheres cyan, capsules yellow; selected entities are shown with the orange selection outline instead, avoiding double strokes.
